issues.body: `workflows_defining_push_skip_job()` scans only `WORKFLOWS.glob("*.yml")`, while GitHub Actions supports both `.yml` and `.yaml`. A future `queue-validated` job added in a `.yaml` file would leave `defining` empty, so `status=blocked` would continue to pass despite the precondition having landed. This contradicts the new documentation's claim that the test checks the live contents of `.github/workflows/` and reds when such a job appears.
issues.fix_hint: Scan both supported extensions (for example, iterate `*.yml` and `*.yaml`) and add a non-vacuity unit fixture/test proving a `.yaml` workflow containing the target job is detected. Prefer testing the scanner against temporary controlled fixtures so the positive path is exercised directly.
issues.title: Push-skip detection ignores valid .yaml workflow files

issues.body: For `status == "applied"`, the test checks only `value > BASELINE`. The file and documentation repeatedly define the authorized edit as exactly `3 -> 5` and `nothing else touched`, but values such as 4, 6, or 999 pass. That makes the coupling pin unable to detect an incorrectly documented applied configuration.
issues.fix_hint: Require `value == APPROVED_TARGET` when status is `applied`, and add explicit tests for the accepted target and rejected non-target values (or factor the state/value validation into a helper that can be tested without rewriting repository files).
issues.title: Applied status does not enforce the approved target value

verdict.summary: The intent is sound, but the new posture gate is not complete enough to support its documented claims. Its workflow scan excludes valid `.yaml` workflow files even though the documentation says it checks all of `.github/workflows/`, and its applied-state check accepts any value above 3 instead of the specifically approved target of 5. Both gaps can let the pin stay green while the repository or documented ruleset posture is wrong.
